question: You are tasked with selecting exactly 2 out of 5 nodes (node_0, node_1, node_2, node_3, node_4) to host facilities, with the goal of maximizing the minimum distance between any two selected facilities. The decision variables are binary: each node can either be selected (1) or not selected (0), and for every pair of nodes, a binary variable indicates whether both nodes in the pair are selected. The distances between nodes are derived from the LP constraints, where the distance between node_0 and node_1 is 18 units (1,000,018 - 1,000,000), node_0 and node_2 is 36 units (1,000,036 - 1,000,000), node_0 and node_3 is 28 units (1,000,028 - 1,000,000), node_0 and node_4 is 20 units (1,000,020 - 1,000,000), node_1 and node_0 is 25 units (1,000,025 - 1,000,000), node_1 and node_2 is 37 units (1,000,037 - 1,000,000), node_1 and node_3 is 36 units (1,000,036 - 1,000,000), node_1 and node_4 is 17 units (1,000,017 - 1,000,000), node_2 and node_0 is 42 units (1,000,042 - 1,000,000), node_2 and node_1 is 42 units (1,000,042 - 1,000,000), node_2 and node_3 is 23 units (1,000,023 - 1,000,000), node_2 and node_4 is 46 units (1,000,046 - 1,000,000), node_3 and node_0 is 31 units (1,000,031 - 1,000,000), node_3 and node_1 is 36 units (1,000,036 - 1,000,000), node_3 and node_2 is 11 units (1,000,011 - 1,000,000), node_3 and node_4 is 50 units (1,000,050 - 1,000,000), node_4 and node_0 is 10 units (1,000,010 - 1,000,000), node_4 and node_1 is 29 units (1,000,029 - 1,000,000), node_4 and node_2 is 24 units (1,000,024 - 1,000,000), and node_4 and node_3 is 42 units (1,000,042 - 1,000,000). The constraints ensure that exactly 2 nodes are selected, and for each pair of nodes, the minimum distance between any two selected facilities must be at least as large as the distance between those two nodes if both nodes in the pair are selected. If either node in the pair is not selected, the constraint is relaxed using a large constant (1,000,000). Additionally, the selection of a pair of nodes is only valid if both nodes in the pair are selected, enforced by ensuring that if a pair is selected, both nodes in the pair must be selected, and if both nodes in a pair are selected, the pair must be selected. The solution must ensure that the facilities are optimally dispersed across the network.

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # --- Sets ---
    model.N = pyo.Set(initialize=d["nodes"], ordered=True)
    # Ordered pairs (i, j) with i != j
    model.P = pyo.Set(
        initialize=[(i, j) for i in d["nodes"] for j in d["nodes"] if i != j],
        dimen=2,
    )

    # Directed distance lookup keyed by the DATA names "dist_i_j"
    def dist(i, j):
        return d["dist_%d_%d" % (i, j)]

    # --- Variables ---
    # x[i] = 1 if node i hosts a facility
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.N, within=pyo.Binary)

    # z[i,j] = 1 if BOTH i and j are selected (pair indicator)
    model.z = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.Binary)

    # w = minimum distance between the two selected facilities (maximized)
    model.w = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # --- Objective: maximize the minimum distance between selected facilities ---
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.w, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # --- Constraints ---

    # Exactly 2 nodes are selected
    def select_rule(m):
        return sum(m.x[i] for i in m.N) == d["K"]
    model.select_exactly_k = pyo.Constraint(rule=select_rule)

    # If pair (i,j) is selected, both i and j must be selected:  z[i,j] <= x[i]
    def pair_le_i_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.z[i, j] <= m.x[i]
    model.pair_le_first = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=pair_le_i_rule)

    # z[i,j] <= x[j]
    def pair_le_j_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.z[i, j] <= m.x[j]
    model.pair_le_second = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=pair_le_j_rule)

    # If both i and j are selected, the pair must be selected: z[i,j] >= x[i]+x[j]-1
    def pair_ge_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.z[i, j] >= m.x[i] + m.x[j] - 1
    model.pair_ge_both = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=pair_ge_rule)

    # Minimum-distance linking (relaxed by big-M when pair not both selected):
    #   w <= dist(i,j) + M * (1 - z[i,j])
    def mindist_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.w <= dist(i, j) + d["M"] * (1 - m.z[i, j])
    model.min_distance = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=mindist_rule)

    return model

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    node_list = d["nodes"]
    distance = d["distance"]
    pair_list = [(i, j) for i in node_list for j in node_list if i != j]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # --- Sets ---
    model.N = pyo.Set(initialize=node_list, ordered=True)
    model.PAIRS = pyo.Set(initialize=pair_list, dimen=2, ordered=True)

    # --- Variables ---
    model.select = pyo.Var(model.N, within=pyo.Binary)
    model.pair_selected = pyo.Var(model.PAIRS, within=pyo.Binary)
    model.min_distance = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # --- Objective: maximise the minimum distance between selected facilities ---
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.min_distance, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # --- Constraint: exactly num_selected nodes are chosen ---
    def exactly_k_rule(m):
        return sum(m.select[i] for i in m.N) == d["num_selected"]

    model.exactly_k = pyo.Constraint(rule=exactly_k_rule)

    # --- Constraint: pair_selected[i,j] <= select[i] ---
    def pair_le_first_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.pair_selected[i, j] <= m.select[i]

    model.pair_le_first = pyo.Constraint(model.PAIRS, rule=pair_le_first_rule)

    # --- Constraint: pair_selected[i,j] <= select[j] ---
    def pair_le_second_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.pair_selected[i, j] <= m.select[j]

    model.pair_le_second = pyo.Constraint(model.PAIRS, rule=pair_le_second_rule)

    # --- Constraint: if both selected, pair must be selected ---
    def pair_ge_both_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.pair_selected[i, j] >= m.select[i] + m.select[j] - 1

    model.pair_ge_both = pyo.Constraint(model.PAIRS, rule=pair_ge_both_rule)

    # --- Constraint: min_distance <= dist[i,j] + M*(1 - pair_selected[i,j]) ---
    def min_distance_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.min_distance <= distance[(i, j)] + d["big_m"] * (1 - m.pair_selected[i, j])

    model.min_distance_con = pyo.Constraint(model.PAIRS, rule=min_distance_rule)

    return model

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    nodes = d["nodes"]
    choose = d["choose"]
    M = d["M"]
    dist = d["dist"]

    # ordered pairs (i, j) with i != j
    pairs = [(i, j) for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.I = pyo.Set(initialize=nodes, ordered=True)
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=pairs, dimen=2, ordered=True)

    # x[i] : node i selected
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.I, within=pyo.Binary)

    # y[i,j] : both i and j selected
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.Binary)

    # z : minimum distance between the two selected facilities
    model.z = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # (1) exactly `choose` nodes selected
    def rule_exactly(m):
        return sum(m.x[i] for i in m.I) == choose
    model.exactly = pyo.Constraint(rule=rule_exactly)

    # (2) y[i,j] <= x[i]
    def rule_pair_le_i(m, i, j):
        return m.y[i, j] <= m.x[i]
    model.pair_le_i = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=rule_pair_le_i)

    # (3) y[i,j] <= x[j]
    def rule_pair_le_j(m, i, j):
        return m.y[i, j] <= m.x[j]
    model.pair_le_j = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=rule_pair_le_j)

    # (4) y[i,j] >= x[i] + x[j] - 1
    def rule_pair_ge(m, i, j):
        return m.y[i, j] >= m.x[i] + m.x[j] - 1
    model.pair_ge = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=rule_pair_ge)

    # (5) z <= dist[i,j] + M*(1 - y[i,j])
    def rule_min_dist(m, i, j):
        return m.z <= dist[(i, j)] + M * (1 - m.y[i, j])
    model.min_dist = pyo.Constraint(model.P, rule=rule_min_dist)

    # objective: maximise the minimum distance between selected facilities
    def rule_obj(m):
        return m.z
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=rule_obj, sense=pyo.maximize)

    return model

    # ---------------- Sets ------------------------------------------------
    m.N = pyo.Set(initialize=d["nodes"])
    m.P = pyo.Set(initialize=d["pairs"], dimen=2)

    # ---------------- Variables -------------------------------------------

    m.x = pyo.Var(m.N, within=pyo.Binary)

    # z[i,j] = 1 if BOTH nodes i and j are selected (pair indicator)
    m.z = pyo.Var(m.P, within=pyo.Binary)

    # r >= 0 is the minimum distance between any two selected facilities
    m.r = pyo.Var(within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # ---------------- Objective -------------------------------------------
    # Maximize the minimum distance between any two selected facilities.
    def obj_rule(mm):
        return mm.r

    m.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.maximize)

    # ---------------- Constraints -----------------------------------------
    # Exactly 2 nodes must be selected.
    def exactly_two_rule(mm):
        return sum(mm.x[i] for i in mm.N) == d["num_select"]

    m.exactly_two = pyo.Constraint(rule=exactly_two_rule)

    # z[i,j] <= x[i]  : if pair (i,j) is selected then i must be selected.
    def pair_implies_i_rule(mm, i, j):
        return mm.z[i, j] <= mm.x[i]

    m.pair_implies_i = pyo.Constraint(m.P, rule=pair_implies_i_rule)

    # z[i,j] <= x[j]  : if pair (i,j) is selected then j must be selected.
    def pair_implies_j_rule(mm, i, j):
        return mm.z[i, j] <= mm.x[j]

    m.pair_implies_j = pyo.Constraint(m.P, rule=pair_implies_j_rule)

    # If both i and j are selected then z[i,j] must be 1:
    #   x[i] + x[j] - 1 <= z[i,j]   ->   z[i,j] >= x[i] + x[j] - 1
    def both_implies_pair_rule(mm, i, j):
        return mm.z[i, j] >= mm.x[i] + mm.x[j] - 1

    m.both_implies_pair = pyo.Constraint(m.P, rule=both_implies_pair_rule)

    # Minimum distance constraint:
    # if pair (i,j) is selected, then r <= distance(i,j);
    # relaxed by big-M when the pair is not selected.
    #   r <= d[i,j] + M * (1 - z[i,j])
    def min_distance_rule(mm, i, j):
        return mm.r <= d["distance_pairs"][i, j] + d["M"] * (1 - mm.z[i, j])

    m.min_distance = pyo.Constraint(m.P, rule=min_distance_rule)

    return m

#               the minimum distance between any two selected facilities.
#

#   maximize   dmin   ("maximizing the minimum distance between any two
#                      selected facilities")
#
# CONSTRAINTS (source-mapped)
#   C1 (count):     sum_i x[i] == K

#   C2 (pair <= x): y[i,j] <= x[i]   for all (i,j)

#                    selected")
#   C3 (pair <= x): y[i,j] <= x[j]   for all (i,j)
#                   (same sentence, other endpoint)
#   C4 (pair >=):   y[i,j] >= x[i] + x[j] - 1   for all (i,j)

#                   ("the minimum distance between any two selected facilities

#                    two nodes if both nodes in the pair are selected; if
#                    either node is not selected the constraint is relaxed
#                    using a large constant M")
